source: methods / Table B2 step 5
assertion: Support seeking through a digital channel is absent from the slow-clock cohorts.
evidence: the construct IS measured in lsac (18 variables), ttm (14 variables), lsic (10 variables). Examples — lsac: hhs55k; hhs55l; hhs55k1; ttm: bhxadvweba; bbhghsq06g; bbhghsq12g; lsic: cse12_12; cse12_13; cse13_12
note: This one is worth acting on. LSAC asks at 14/15 and 16/17 y whether the young person sought help from the internet or a phone help line, and Ten to Men and LSIC ask the same in a comparable form. That is a coarse binary source endorsement rather than the maintaining mechanism, so it cannot substitute for WP2 and WP3 — but it is a harmonisable cross-cohort proxy for digital help seeking, and claiming its absence understates what three cohorts already hold.
